page: Amazon Web Services a1.2xlarge is an ARM-based server instance powered by the first-generation AWS Graviton processor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs utilizing the ARMv8 Cortex-A72 architecture running at 2.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or GPU hardware. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the a1.2xlarge delivers average results for compute-heavy workloads but exhibits limitations in memory-intensive tasks. In stress-ng testing, single-core and multi-core CPU performance scored in the average range, with 1491.99 and 11904.08 respectively. However, memory bandwidth is weak, with read-only large block speeds at 23.51 GB/sec and write speeds at 8.88 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks also show lower relative performance, as evidenced by a poor rating in single-threaded gzip compression and PassMark CPU encryption tests.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the a1.2xlarge offers an entry-level ARM64 development environment with dedicated physical cores, avoiding hyperthreading overhead. However, the lack of advanced vector extensions (AVX) and lower memory throughput represent significant tradeoffs. This instance is best suited for scale-out workloads that benefit from physical core isolation, such as basic web serving, containerized microservices, and ARM64 software compilation.
